title: Template Argument Deduction
learningObjectives: Identify template parameters and required operations.
Design a reusable generic utility or type.

understand.concept: Template argument deduction infers template types from function argument patterns. When two arguments must deduce the same type, mixed types may cause deduction conflicts. Explicit template arguments can resolve intent.
understand.whyItMatters: Deduction reduces call-site syntax while preserving compile-time type checking.
understand.explain: Compare inferred calls and explicit calls. When deduction conflicts, use a design with distinct template parameters or explicitly specify the intended type.

examples.title: Deduced int
examples.code: template<class T>T twice(T x){return x+x;}\nint n=twice(4);

examples.title: Deduced double
examples.code: template<class T>T twice(T x){return x+x;}\ndouble d=twice(1.5);

examples.title: Deduction conflict
examples.code: template<class T>T add(T a,T b){return a+b;}\n// add(2,2.5) can fail deduction
examples.explanation: Both arguments try to deduce the same T.

examples.title: Explicit type
examples.code: template<class T>T twice(T x){return x+x;}\ndouble d=twice<double>(2);
examples.explanation: Caller explicitly selects T as double.

examples.title: Const reference deduction
examples.explanation: T is deduced while const reference avoids a copy.

practise.guidedTask: Analyze each Template Argument Deduction example: identify parameters, requirements, deduced or explicit arguments, and instantiated behavior.
practise.independentTask: Write a generic C++ utility or type demonstrating template argument deduction. Test two supported types, one boundary case, and one unsupported/constrained type; explain why it is or is not accepted.
hints: Begin with a concrete example before generalizing.
Name template parameters for their roles.

questions.explanation: Template deduction matches arguments to parameter patterns.
Same type parameter may be deduced inconsistently.
